Gun Wings, developed by Mercury Stone, Angels Blue Digital Entertainment, and DigitalEZ, and published by DigitalEZ, is a vertical scrolling shoot ’em up that successfully combines nostalgic arcade-style gameplay with modern touches to create an engaging and challenging experience. The game sets itself in a futuristic world where humanity faces an impending meteorite threat, and players take control of three cybernetically enhanced young women tasked with saving Earth from destruction. This premise provides a straightforward but compelling backdrop that drives the action forward and immerses players in a high-stakes battle across visually rich environments.

The core gameplay of Gun Wings revolves around navigating dense waves of enemies and intricate bullet patterns, a hallmark of the shoot ’em up genre. Players select from three distinct protagonists, each equipped with unique weapons and abilities that cater to different playstyles. The controls are tight and responsive, allowing for precise maneuvers essential to dodging the relentless barrage of enemy fire. Throughout six stages, players encounter increasingly complex enemy formations and formidable bosses, requiring not only quick reflexes but also strategic use of each character’s skills. This blend of accessibility and depth makes Gun Wings appealing both to veteran shmup players and those new to the genre looking for a satisfying challenge.

Visually, Gun Wings strikes a balance between vibrant, colorful aesthetics and a futuristic setting that feels alive and dynamic. The character designs are detailed and anime-inspired, contributing to the game’s distinctive personality, while the backgrounds and enemy sprites feature enough variety to keep the visual experience fresh. The bullet patterns are particularly well-designed, combining beauty with function — the intricate arrangements of projectiles form mesmerizing patterns that are both obstacles and spectacles. Although the game doesn’t boast cutting-edge graphics, its art style suits the gameplay perfectly, enhancing the overall atmosphere without overwhelming the player.

The soundtrack and audio design further amplify the game’s intensity and immersive quality. Gun Wings features energetic, upbeat tracks that match the pace of the action, providing a pulse-pounding soundtrack that pushes players to stay engaged through each stage. The sound effects for weapons, explosions, and power-ups are crisp and satisfying, adding tactile feedback to every encounter. While some may find the music loops somewhat repetitive over extended play, the compositions are generally effective at maintaining the game’s momentum and excitement.

From a technical standpoint, Gun Wings performs well across a range of systems, including those with modest hardware, thanks to its optimized design. The game offers support for both keyboard and controller inputs, catering to player preferences and enhancing accessibility. Additional features such as Steam achievements, cloud saves, and leaderboards contribute to the replay value, encouraging players to refine their skills and compete for high scores. These elements, while standard, are thoughtfully implemented and help sustain player interest beyond the initial playthrough.

Though Gun Wings does not reinvent the shoot ’em up wheel, it delivers a polished, enjoyable experience that pays homage to classic arcade shooters while incorporating modern sensibilities. Its combination of challenging gameplay, attractive visuals, and an engaging soundtrack make it a solid choice for fans of the genre or anyone seeking an adrenaline-fueled, skill-based action game. Whether you’re a seasoned shmup enthusiast or a newcomer eager to dive into fast-paced aerial combat, Gun Wings offers a compelling journey filled with excitement and nostalgic charm.

Rating: 8/10

A surprisingly beautiful game when you actually play it. The game's title bar actually does the game a disservice with it's garish over-saturated tri-colour characters. The moment you boot up the game you are met with a beautiful rust-punk aesthetic with a very well coordinated colour palate. Game is fun too. It uses the same hold & release system that Vukaiser uses, but with 2 levels to charge up, instead of just one. There's also a separate attack that charges very slowly by killing enemies that you lose when you lose a life which helps add tension. I still think it would be better if you didn't have to hold the button down to attack, but that can probably be fixed with something like anitmicrox.

事实上，我愿意给出好评超过90%的因素在于这是一款国产STG游戏，在赤过《雷霆战机》那一坨之后才会觉得这款游戏已经弥足珍贵。如果th20（东方系列第20作）以这样的质量呈现的话，我可能会忍不住赶赴日本例大祭当面攻击ZUN。
       怎么说呢……立绘很好看，嗯（保命，没有任何拉踩的意思，ZUN绘天下第一）；我不确定有没有忽略什么部分，但是剧情似乎略显单薄，如果像我所看到的只有开头设定和结尾一样？明明三个少女的设计看起来都有自己特色的说（或者也许是什么其他我还没有玩过的作品里有做人设？），总觉得应该有些对话什么的。音乐方面中规中矩，就是普通的STG配乐吧。
       嗯，是的，那些并不那么重要的东西说完了，然后……就来到了有点难以启齿的部分。我可以理解对一个主打视觉小说（应该是？玩过好几作蓝天使出品的VN）的工作室来说，制作一款STG游戏其实是一个很大胆的创新举措，缺乏经验是必然的；我猜测工作室内部应该也存在喜爱STG游戏的同好……？但是至少，在推出一款操作类游戏之前，适当的测试是必要的，“反正允许了无限续关，玩家怎么样都可以通关的，我也达不到真正大神的水平，所以高难度的弹幕设计简单地把几个参数调上去、把简单难度的弹幕随便复杂化一下就好啦”这种想法绝对是不负责任的。Easy和Normal两个难度虽然跨度较大，对于有相当STG基础的玩家来说，也还算可以接受，最底层弹幕原型的设计应该还是人工测试或者至少审查过的。但是，我相当怀疑制作团队是否亲手完整测试过Nightmare级别的难度，因为过于大段的内容已经让人几乎感受不到属于STG游戏的任何乐趣——那种想方设法寻求策略、一点点突破自我极限或是尽可能效率最大化配置资源的乐趣；如果最高难度只有1、2面，至多达到3面，我还可以认为作者可能有着巅峰时期ZUN甚至更高的水平，毕竟不讨论手感和视觉问题的话，1面充其量也就是大部分th作品L难度3、4面左右的水平，2面背板也可以作为一个对标较长的L难度5面。然而，从三面开始难度就已经开始畸高，非消弹机体几乎每一个大段落都要靠Bomb或者蓄力攻击度过、消弹机体同样也只能勉强求生；而四面开始难度进一步上升，同时大量弹幕速度已经到了不可理喻的地步；到达5、6面的绝大部分弹幕内容，玩家几乎可以只把手放在X与C两个键上，只要理解自机狙是什么的玩家，操作起来没有任何区别，要么消弹要么神穿，miss了就补充两个bomb。这样的弹幕设计让我看不到任何的意义，从实际结果来说与设计若干束激光墙从上而下扫过几乎没有任何区别，这不是我所理解的STG游戏应有的样子——所以你让我聚精会神盯着一堵墙费什么劲呢？也许不知道多少年后“武器少女”形式的AI统治人类后会认为这才是一部可以称之为神作的STG作品，它只是出现得过于超前于这个时代了而已？（好吧虽然实际上打到后面我的反应是“哈哈哈这个游戏实在是太好玩了，我一定要把它推荐给我所有的朋友，然后我的朋友再推荐给朋友的朋友哈哈哈哈哈哈哈”）
       最后，还是提一点体验上的问题。手感问题很多评论提过，对于这个大小的弹幕和缝隙来说精度过低了一点；此外，蓄力攻击和bomb的机制实在是过于不友好了。鉴于bomb并没有设计决死判定也并不存在无敌帧（是的这一点曾经让我十分恼火，当那个叫做“殉弹”的鬼成就跳出来之后，但是也许是我几乎只打东方的锅按下不表），我们是否至少应该在两种消弹即将结束的时刻通过动画和音效做出提醒？毕竟没有人会在依然需要担心密集弹幕存在漏网之鱼的时候选择冒险去看左下角；一些直接生成在下半区的弹幕是否至少应该有一定的预先警示？开着bomb忽然被刷脸的感觉一点也不好，虽然作者可能会觉得偶然皮一下很开心。
      总的来说，其实是一部让人犹豫是否推荐的游戏。可以感觉到制作组应该是向其中投入了相当的心血的（顺带一提还有换装小彩蛋来着，不过不太知道怎么触发的），并且确实在许多部分有着让人不忍差评的精致。考虑到这款游戏价格并不算高并且可以通过Bundle进一步降价，体验Easy与Normal难度并观赏几遍Hard难度也许是值得的

Gun Wings is the perfect blend of bullet hell chaos and anime aesthetic, with a story that throws you right into the action. The year is 2117, and humanity's fate rests in the hands of three cybernetically modified girls, sent to destroy a meteorite carrying unknown life forms and deadly viruses. The game’s intense difficulty is balanced with fast-paced action and gorgeous visuals, making every run feel exciting. The female protagonists bring that anime flair, while the soundtrack enhances the immersion.

Kawaii Factor Breakdown:
★ Character Design: 9/10 – The cybernetic girls are stylish, but there’s room for even more customization.
★ Bullet Hell Intensity: 10/10 – It’s chaotic, it’s fast, and you’ll be dodging for your life every second.
★ Soundtrack: 8/10 – Really brings out the atmosphere of the futuristic world and high-stakes action.
★ Difficulty: 10/10 – Prepare to be challenged. This is not a game for casuals.

Pro Tips:
- Focus on learning attack patterns early on, the difficulty spikes fast.
- Take advantage of the girls’ unique abilities to maneuver through the toughest sections.
- Master the bullet-jumping mechanic for precision dodging in tight spots.

Final Verdict:
Gun Wings is a must-play for fans of bullet hell shooters and anime lovers alike. The combination of fast-paced, high-stakes gameplay, anime characters, and an epic, apocalyptic storyline keeps the tension high. With plenty of challenge and beautifully designed levels, it’s a rewarding experience for anyone looking to test their reflexes and skills.

Avec son approche classique, Gun Wings propose un gameplay efficace qui fera le bonheur des amateurs du genre. Pas véritablement nerveux au sens propre du terme, il n'en reste pas moins plaisant manette en main. Son système de couleurs est courant sur ce type de jeu et offre une échappatoire bienvenue aux plus adroits. Proposant plusieurs modes de difficulté, celle-ci est progressive et bien dosée. Coloré, le jeu manque cependant d'animations sur les décors et les ennemis. L'ambiance musicale et les effets sonores sont réussis et fonctionnent bien. J'aime beaucoup le système de points proposé et le jeu invite au scoring. Certes, il n'offre rien de nouveau et s'appuie sur des mécaniques éprouvées, mais il le fait bien.
